proof:
A point missing the first two halfplanes satisfies $x+y\le-2/100<1/100$ and belongs to the third. The area of $K$ is half the product of its horizontal base of length $11$ and height $5$. Each cutting line isolates one vertex, giving relative areas equal to products of the intercept fractions along its two incident edges. At $(7,-2)$ the factors for the first cap are $(701/100)/11$ and $(701/100)/9$; at $(-2,3)$ those for the second are both $(301/100)/5$; at $(-4,-2)$ those for the third are $(601/100)/11$ and $(601/100)/7$. These give the three claimed fractions.

The common intersection is the right triangle of leg $3/100$ with vertices $(-1/100,-1/100)$, $(2/100,-1/100)$, and $(-1/100,2/100)$, up to its boundary. These vertices lie in $K$: its defining inequalities are $y\ge-2$, $5x-2y\ge-16$, and $5x+9y\le17$, and all three points satisfy them strictly. Its area is $9/20000$, giving common fraction $9/550000$. If $F_1,F_2,F_3$ are the area fractions covered once, twice, and three times, then $F_1+F_2+F_3=1$ and the sum of cap fractions is $F_1+2F_2+3F_3$. Subtracting gives $F_1=2-230051893/173250000+9/550000=58225471/86625000$. Direct subtraction gives the stated excess over half the sum. The three cap fractions are strictly below $(705/1000)^2$, $(603/1000)^2$, and $(685/1000)^2$, respectively, by integer cross-multiplication. Hence $\sum_i\sqrt{A_i/M}<1993/1000<2$, making the proposed right-hand side negative while the common area is positive.

statement: In $K=\operatorname{conv}\{(-4,-2),(7,-2),(-2,3)\}$ of area $55/2$, the three open halfplanes $x>-1/100$, $y>-1/100$, and $x+y<1/100$ cover the plane. Their cap fractions in $K$ are respectively $491401/990000$, $90601/250000$, $361201/770000$, each strictly below $1/2$, and their sum is $230051893/173250000<4/3$. The fraction covered by exactly one is $58225471/86625000>2/3$, exceeding half their summed cap fractions by $949997/115500000$. The common intersection has area $9/20000$. With $A_i$ the cap areas and $M=|K|$, this example also refutes the unequal-mass square-root inequality $\sqrt{|K\cap U_1\cap U_2\cap U_3|}\le\sum_i\sqrt{A_i}-2\sqrt M$.
title: Three unequal planar caps can exceed two-thirds exclusive area
